description:
## Why

Storing articles as raw .eml files in a Maildir hierarchy makes the stoa archive accessible to any Maildir-compatible tool: notmuch, neomutt, alot, astroid, emacs notmuch-mode, offlineimap, mbsync, etc. For personal/hobbyist deployments this is a significant quality-of-life improvement — users get their existing MUA workflows over their NNTP subscriptions without any additional tooling.

It also makes the block store human-inspectable and recoverable with standard Unix tools, unlike LMDB or SQLite blobs.

## What

Implement MaildirBlockStore for crates/reader/src/post/ and crates/transit/src/peering/ implementing IpfsBlockStore / IpfsStore respectively.

**Storage layout:**
Each newsgroup maps to a Maildir folder:
```
<root>/
  comp.lang.rust/
    cur/    — delivered messages
    new/    — newly arrived messages
    tmp/    — in-progress writes
  comp.os.linux/
    cur/
    new/
    tmp/
```

Group name dots map directly to the Maildir folder name (no subdirectory splitting — notmuch handles flat group names fine).

Each article is stored as a single .eml file in new/ on write, using a standard Maildir unique name: `<timestamp>.<pid>.<hostname>`. No flags suffix on initial write.

**CID mapping:** A SQLite sidecar database (maildir_index.db) in the root directory maps CID → (group, maildir_filename). Required because Maildir filenames are not CIDs.

**Config:**
- maildir.root — path to the Maildir root directory
- maildir.group_source — how to determine which group folder to write to: from the Newsgroups header (default) or a fixed folder name

## Implementation notes

- put_raw: compute CID, write to tmp/, rename to new/<unique-name>, record CID→path in SQLite sidecar
- put_block: same but with caller-supplied CID
- get_raw: look up path in SQLite sidecar, read file
- delete: look up path, remove file, remove sidecar row
- All blocking I/O via spawn_blocking
- Atomic write via tmp/→new/ rename (same pattern as FsBlockStore)

## Acceptance

- MaildirBlockStore implements IpfsBlockStore
- Written files are valid Maildir (notmuch new indexes them without error)
- Round-trip put/get/delete tests pass
- CID→path mapping survives process restart
- Config accepts [backend.maildir] section
notes: Does not handle notmuch tags or JMAP keyword sync — that is stoa-maildir-notmuch-tags (filed separately and depends on this issue).
title: Maildir block store backend
